transport: RS-232 / RS-485 / TTL · Modbus RTU · 9600 8N1 · slave address held in 0x001A, range 1–247 (0x00 broadcast, 0xFF answers regardless of configured address); the doc's worked example reads 1 and three implementations use 1, but no factory default is stated
blocks: 0x000A–0x001A device identity · 0x0100–0x0122 real-time, today's extremes, lifetime counters, faults · 0xE001–0xE021 EEPROM settings · 0xF000–0xF3FF one 20-byte block per past day

downgradedOnReview: The register map itself is real and shared — but the claim as written overstates it in three ways, one of which is a bench hazard.  WHAT SURVIVES. The committed PDF at /Users/lemarier/dev/solar/docs/srne-modbus-protocol-v3.9.pdf exists, MD5 ce84b5f61a396bc56733cb1ea57342ff matches as cited. It carries exactly one PDU address table (Section 3, pages 11-19), no per-model variants. Section 2.3 note 2 is quoted verbatim-
gotchas: 9600 baud, not 115200. Anyone carrying habits over from the EPEver driver in this repo will see silence on an otherwise correct wiring.

0x0102 is charging current INTO the battery. It is unsigned and cannot express a bank being discharged. Unlike EPEver, this map has no bidirectional battery-current register anywhere — battery-current from this dialect is charge-only, and battery-power cannot be derived truthfully.

0x0103 packs two temperatures into one word: high byte = controller internal, low byte = battery. Each is sign-magnitude (b7 = sign, b0–b6 = magnitude), NOT two's complement. Negative battery temperatures decode wrong under a naive i16 read.

0x0120 packs load on/off and brightness into the high byte (b7 = load state, b0–b6 = brightness 0x00–0x64) and charge state into the low byte. Both cole8888 and Tolyak26 handle this by subtracting 32768 when the word exceeds 6 — that is wrong for any brightness other than 0 or 100. Mask with 0xFF for charge state and s

Writing 0x010A to switch the load only takes effect after 0xE01D has been set to 0x0F (manual mode) — doc §4.16. A set-switch that silently does nothing is the expected failure if the controller is still in light-control mode.
unmappedReports: daily minimum and maximum battery voltage (0x010B, 0x010C), daily maximum charging and discharging current (0x010D, 0x010E), daily maximum charging and discharging power (0x010F, 0x0110), daily charging and discharging amp-hours (0x0111, 0x0112), lifetime charging and discharging amp-hours (0x0118–0x0119, 0x011A–0x011B), DC load energy today and lifetime (0x0114, 0x011E–0x011F) — ac-energy-today/ac-energy-total are AC-only, and there is no DC equivalent, controller internal temperature (0x0103 high byte) — `temperature` is documented as ambient, which this is not, total days in service (0x0115), battery over-discharge count (0x0116) and full-charge count (0x0117) — neither is `cycle-count`, street-light load brightness percent (0x0120 high byte, b0–b6), controller fault and alarm bitfield (0x0121 high 16, 0x0122 low 16) — roughly 25 defined flags with no MetricKind and no event kind to carry them, battery type setting (0xE004: 0 self-customised, 1 open, 2 sealed, 3 gel, 4 lithium), configured system voltage and rated charge/discharge current (0x000A, 0x000B), product model ASCII string, software version, hardware version, serial number (0x000C–0x0019), nominal battery capacity setting in Ah (0xE002), load working mode (0xE01D) and light-control delay / voltage (0xE01E, 0xE01F), per-day historical blocks for up to 1024 past days (0xF000–0xF3FF)
